title: Tools for the Field Kit
story:
FIELD KIT PACKING LIST, laminated, signed I. Halvorsen.
[x] Boots, two pairs
[x] Satellite phone
[ ] `curl`, to poll the weather feed
[ ] `jq`, to read what the feed sends back

The last two are software. The field laptops run a container image, and plain `alpine:3.20` ships with neither tool. Build `kestrel/fieldkit:1.0` on top of `alpine:3.20` with both installed. Alpine's package manager is `apk`, and the satellite link is slow, so keep the image under 30 MB.
objectives: Write `/workspace/Dockerfile` based on `alpine:3.20` that installs `curl` and `jq` with `apk`
Build the image as `kestrel/fieldkit:1.0` and keep it under 30 MB
startingState: An empty /workspace. The machine has internet access for downloading Alpine packages.
hints: Installing software while building an image is done with a `RUN` instruction, which executes a command during the build and saves the result in the image.
On Alpine the install command is `apk add`. Add `--no-cache` so the package index is not stored in the image, and list both tools in one `RUN` line.

```bash
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM alpine:3.20
RUN apk add --no-cache curl jq
EOF
docker build -t kestrel/fieldkit:1.0 .
docker run --rm kestrel/fieldkit:1.0 jq --version
```

validation.description: The image is smaller than 30 MB

solution:
cat > Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM alpine:3.20
RUN apk add --no-cache curl jq
EOF
debrief: `RUN` executes during the build and bakes the result into a new layer, and `--no-cache` keeps apk's index files out of that layer. Pro tip: combine related installs in one `RUN` so they share a single layer.
